The aircraft landed safely with no fatalities or major injuries to passengers and crew.  An NTSB investigation found that the incident was caused by a failure in the fuselage skin due to metal fatigue.

On landing, the aircraft struck an earth bank which ripped off all three undercarriage legs, and came to rest on its belly with an engine on fire.  One of the sixteen passengers suffered minor injuries.  The aircraft was written off.
Southwest Airlines Flight 345 | Southwest Airlines Flight 345 was a scheduled flight from Nashville International Airport to New York City's LaGuardia Airport on July 22, 2013.  The Boeing 737 suffered a collapse of its front landing gear while landing at LaGuardia Airport, injuring 9 people on board.  The aircraft, which was worth an estimated $15.5 million at the time, was written off as a total loss and scrapped as a result of the accident.
Eastern Airlines Flight 935 | Eastern Airlines Flight 935 was a scheduled commercial passenger flight operated by Eastern Airlines.  On September 22, 1981, Eastern Airlines Flight 935, a Lockheed L-1011 TriStar jet suffered an uncontained engine failure which led to a loss of 3 out of the 4 hydraulic systems aboard the aircraft at an altitude of 10000 ft MSL.  The crew were able to land the aircraft safely to an emergency landing at John F. Kennedy International Airport with some limited use of the outboard spoilers, the inboard ailerons and the horizontal stabilizer, plus differential engine power of the remaining two engines.
